articles.title: US Open accused of 'corruption' after handing Venus Williams a wild card
articles.standfirst: The seven-time Grand Slam champion's place in the New York draw has sparked criticism over whether reputation is outweighing merit
articles.summary: The seven-time Grand Slam champion's place in the New York draw has sparked criticism over whether reputation is outweighing merit
articles.body:
Venus Williams ' return to the US Open has triggered a fierce debate after the 46-year-old received a wild card into the women's singles draw, with one tennis insider going as far as describing the decision as "corrupt."

Williams remains one of the most recognizable players in the history of the sport, but her ranking and limited recent match activity meant she needed an invitation from organizers to compete in New York.

The USTA ultimately gave her one, allowing the two-time US Open champion to return to a tournament where she first reached the final in 1997.

However, the decision has reopened a wider argument about how Grand Slam wild cards are distributed and whether younger players with stronger recent results are being denied opportunities because tournaments prefer famous names.

US Open wild card decision comes under fire

The criticism centers less on Williams personally than on the system used to award discretionary places in major tournaments.

One tennis insider argued that the process has become too dependent on profile, marketability and relationships rather than current sporting merit, describing the situation as "corrupt."

That is a serious accusation, although there is no suggestion that the US Open broke any formal rule by selecting Williams . Tournament organizers are allowed to award wild cards at their discretion, and former champions have routinely benefited from that flexibility.

Williams also brings obvious commercial appeal, particularly in New York, where she and sister Serena Williams became central figures in one of tennis' most successful eras.

Debate goes beyond Venus Williams

The uncomfortable question is whether that history should continue carrying more weight than the current form of players trying to establish themselves.

Wild cards can provide vital opportunities for young Americans, returning players and competitors whose rankings don't reflect their ability because of injury. Every place given to an established star therefore means one fewer opening for somebody else.

Williams ' record makes her case more compelling than most. She has won seven Grand Slam singles titles, including the US Open in 2000 and 2001, and remains one of the sport's defining figures.

Still, critics argue that prestige shouldn't make wild cards automatic indefinitely.

The controversy has therefore become bigger than one veteran receiving one invitation.

Williams will attract enormous attention when she returns to Flushing Meadows, which is precisely why the US Open wanted her there.

Whether that makes the decision commercially sensible or competitively unfair depends on what fans believe a wild card is supposed to reward.

articles.title: US Open 2026 schedule: Dates, times and where to watch the Grand Slam from New York
articles.standfirst: The final Grand Slam of the season begins August 30, with two weeks of singles action leading to the men's final on September 13
articles.summary: The final Grand Slam of the season begins August 30, with two weeks of singles action leading to the men's final on September 13
articles.body:
The 2026 US Open will bring another packed fortnight of Grand Slam tennis to New York , with the main draw running from Sunday, August 30 through Sunday, September 13 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center.

First round matches begin on August 30 and continue through September 1, with day sessions starting at 11 a.m. ET and night sessions generally beginning at 7 p.m. ET.

The second round follows on September 2 and 3, before the third-round matches take place on September 4 and 5. The round of 16 is scheduled across September 6 and 7.

Quarterfinals then begin on September 8 as the tournament moves toward its championship weekend.

When are the 2026 US Open finals?

The women's semifinals are scheduled for Thursday, September 10, beginning at 7 p.m. ET.

The men's semifinals take place the following day, with the first scheduled for 3 p.m. ET and the second beginning at 7 p.m. ET.

The women's singles final will be played on Saturday, September 12 at 4 p.m. ET, before the men's championship match brings the tournament to a close on Sunday, September 13 at 2 p.m. ET.

Exact match times during earlier rounds can change once the daily order of play is released.

Where can you watch the 2026 US Open?

ESPN remains the exclusive US broadcaster for the US Open under its long-term agreement with the USTA.

Television coverage will be spread across ESPN, ESPN2 and ABC, while ESPN's digital platforms will provide extensive streaming throughout the tournament.

Beginning in 2026, ESPN's expanded agreement also brings additional US Open streaming coverage, with every match and court available through the ESPN App for eligible subscribers.

ESPN Deportes provides Spanish language coverage in the United States, while TSN and RDS continue carrying the tournament in Canada.

The 2026 tournament begins with three days of first round singles matches before progressing toward championship weekend.

Day sessions during the opening week generally start at 11 a.m. ET, while the main night sessions begin around 7 p.m. ET at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

That gives fans nearly two full weeks of action before the champions are crowned.

The key dates are September 12 for the women's final and September 13 for the men's final, with New York once again providing the stage for the final Grand Slam titles of the season.

articles.title: 'Actually scandalous': US Open ticket prices skyrocket, leaving fans fuming over seatless passes
articles.standfirst: The cost of watching tennis in New York has surged, leaving ordinary fans questioning whether the Grand Slam is becoming a luxury event
articles.summary: The cost of watching tennis in New York has surged, leaving ordinary fans questioning whether the Grand Slam is becoming a luxury event
articles.body:
The US Open is almost here, and while anticipation is building for tennis’ final Grand Slam of the year, fans are facing an unwelcome hurdle: eye-watering ticket prices.

The 2026 tournament officially gets underway with Fan Week on August 23, while the singles main draw begins August 30 at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in Flushing Meadows. The event runs through September 13.

With stars including Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka expected in New York, demand is high. But according to figures circulating this week, the average resale price for entry has climbed significantly compared with the same point last year.

A particularly striking example is the reported $363 price for a grounds pass on the tournament’s opening day. That’s a steep amount for a ticket that doesn’t guarantee a seat inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Officially, grounds admission provides first-come, first-served access to general-admission areas in Louis Armstrong Stadium, the Grandstand and the outer courts.

It doesn’t include access to Arthur Ashe, meaning buyers could spend hundreds of dollars without having a reserved seat for the tournament’s biggest matches.

The USTA has also increased the face value of a grounds pass from $60 to $65 this year, although resale demand has pushed some tickets dramatically higher.

Fans question whether the Open is becoming too exclusive

The price gap with other Grand Slam events has fueled even more frustration.

A grounds pass at Wimbledon during the opening week was reportedly around $44.70, while Roland Garros admission was roughly $45. Tickets for the 2027 Australian Open have also been reported at around $35.

Fans have taken to social media to criticize what they see as an increasingly inaccessible tournament. Some have recalled paying roughly $50 for a grounds pass years ago and enjoying an entire day of tennis, moving from court to court without spending a fortune.

Others have questioned whether corporate allocations and influencer attendance have contributed to an atmosphere where ordinary tennis fans are being pushed aside.

One prominent critic called the pricing “actually scandalous,” while another argued that the event is becoming an experience for “the rich and well connected.”

The controversy comes despite uncertainty surrounding two of the sport’s biggest attractions. Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner both withdrew from the Cincinnati Open with injuries, raising questions about their US Open preparations.

Alcaraz , the defending champion, has been sidelined since April but has recently been seen training on hard courts.

Despite those concerns, demand hasn’t appeared to weaken. TicketData’s Keith Pagello said prices continued rising even after both withdrawals.

With the tournament approaching, the debate is now about more than ticket prices and more about whether the US Open is still an event they can realistically afford to experience in person.

articles.title: Serena Williams sends message to Carlos Alcaraz sparking rumors ahead of the US Open
articles.standfirst: Instagram comment revived speculation over a potential partnership
articles.summary: Instagram comment revived speculation over a potential partnership
articles.body:
The biggest question around Carlos Alcaraz had been whether his injured wrist would allow him to return in time for the US Open . Now that he has confirmed his comeback, attention has quickly shifted to whether Serena Williams could be waiting to join him.

Alcaraz announced his return with a social media video and the message, “We’re back, Here we Go.”

Then Williams stepped in. “Ohhhhh ok. I like seeing this,” the 23-time Grand Slam champion commented.

It was only six words, but given the speculation already surrounding the pair, the response was enough to send tennis fans back into detective mode.

Nothing has been officially announced. Still, Williams has previously interacted with Alcaraz ’s recovery posts, and another message linked to the rumors — “They are not ready” — only strengthened the sense that something could be developing behind the scenes.

Why an Alcaraz-Williams team feels possible

The timing works in a way it did not a few weeks ago. Alcaraz has been sidelined since April because of a wrist injury and withdrew from both the French Open and Wimbledon rather than risk worsening the problem.

His absence from Cincinnati created another layer of uncertainty over whether he would even be ready for New York. That changed with his latest announcement.

The US Open mixed doubles tournament is scheduled for August 24-26 and still had wildcard places available in the supplied information.

The event has been deliberately built around star power, with Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka among the high-profile names already linked in teams.

A pairing involving Williams and Alcaraz would fit that philosophy almost perfectly. It would also create one of the biggest attractions of the tournament before the singles draw even begins.

A useful test before singles

The pairing wouldn't be valuable only as a spectacle. Alcaraz hasn't competed in more than four months, meaning the challenge in New York goes well beyond simply being healthy enough to swing a racket again.

The shortened mixed doubles format could give him competitive repetitions without immediately exposing him to the demands of a five-set singles match.

Before the injury, Alcaraz had been in excellent form, winning 22 of 25 matches and claiming titles at the Australian Open and in Doha.

He also enters the US Open with significant ranking pressure. Alcaraz remains No.2 and has 2,000 points to defend, while Jannik Sinner holds a sizeable advantage at the top.

Williams , meanwhile, has already returned to competition this summer and has played doubles alongside Venus Williams , which gives the rumor another layer of plausibility.

Until the remaining mixed doubles teams are officially announced, though, that is all it remains: a rumor. But after Alcaraz confirmed his return and Williams immediately responded, the possibility no longer feels quite so far-fetched.

articles.title: US Open 2026 Tickets: How much are tickets for the US Grand Slam?
articles.standfirst: Fans can still find cheaper options, but premium seats are reaching huge numbers
articles.summary: Fans can still find cheaper options, but premium seats are reaching huge numbers
articles.body:
The US Open has become one of the biggest sporting spectacles in the world, combining elite tennis with New York entertainment, celebrity appearances and a festival-like atmosphere.

However, fans hoping to watch the 2026 Grand Slam in person will face a major question before making plans which is how much will tickets actually cost?

The tournament begins on Tuesday, August 25, at the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center , with 128 men and 128 women competing for one of tennis’ most prestigious titles.

Defending champions Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka headline a star-studded field that includes Novak Djokovic, Coco Gauff, Iga Swiatek, Jannik Sinner, Alexander Zverev and Jessica Pegula .

Ticket prices vary significantly depending on the session, stadium and location, with some options remaining accessible while premium seats have reached record levels.

Cheapest US Open 2026 tickets and what fans can expect to pay

Fans looking for the lowest-cost way to attend the tournament can find tickets starting around $49 , including fees, for certain sessions on resale platforms.

Some general admission grounds passes and other events have been listed from around $23, although availability and prices can change as the tournament approaches.

Grounds passes provide access to the wider USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center , allowing fans to watch matches on outside courts and experience the atmosphere around the venue.

However, they don't guarantee entry into Arthur Ashe Stadium , where the biggest matches are played. The biggest price increases have been seen around high-demand sessions.

Some resale listings for opening-week grounds passes have climbed above $360 , despite face-value prices being much lower.

Arthur Ashe Stadium tickets are also commanding premium prices.

Upper-level seats have reached several hundred dollars, while lower sections closer to the court can cost more than $500 . Some premium hospitality and courtside options have reached thousands of dollars.

The increase comes as the US Open continues a major transformation of Arthur Ashe Stadium , with an $800 million renovation project designed to add upgraded seating and hospitality areas.

Why are US Open tickets becoming so expensive?

The rising cost of attending the US Open is linked to several factors, including increased demand for live sports, the popularity of tennis among younger audiences and the growth of the secondary ticket market.

The tournament has become more than just a tennis event, attracting celebrities, athletes and entertainment figures while creating a unique New York experience.

USTA chief commercial officer Kirsten Corio defended the organization’s approach, pointing to efforts such as Fan Week, which allows fans to attend qualifying matches, practices and other events at lower prices.

“You could see Djokovic on Arthur Ashe playing a practice match against another top-10 player for free in the first row,” Corio said. “That’s like no other sport that I can think of.”

The 2026 US Open will also feature special attractions outside the main tournament.

A legends exhibition featuring Roger Federer, John McEnroe, Andre Agassi and Andy Roddick will take place on August 25, while The Lumineers will perform during the tournament’s opening events.

Federer said returning to Arthur Ashe Stadium would be a meaningful experience.

“So many unforgettable moments of my career happened in New York, and Arthur Ashe Stadium is a place that means a great deal to me,” Federer said.

With some cheaper options still available but premium seats becoming increasingly expensive, fans will need to decide how much they are willing to spend to experience one of tennis’ biggest stages.
